solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Item of mail getting new staff very upset in middle of week

indicators.note: the new-staff-very group sits inside the central letters of the word week
the middle of week is its central pair of letters
in a down clue upset means the words staff and very are turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A worker grumbling about new staff upsetting the office mid-week.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns staff-plus-very upside down, giving VELOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A posted letter-holder is a piece of stationery that travels through the post, an item of mail.

clue.text: Shelter? You'll find in this some purpose

parts.words: You'll find in this some purpose
parts.note: put the word in before this word and you get a word meaning purpose or aim

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a shelter has any purpose at all.
explanation.walkthrough: IN followed by this answer spells INTENT, purpose: 'in this' is literal instruction rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas camping shelter is a simple, portable form of shelter.

clue.text: Permit to travel hard to extract from plane group

indicators.note: extracting from a word means taking the hard letter out of it

parts.note: a thicket is a dense group of trees, such as plane trees
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A travel permit that is hard to get out of an aircraft crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane group' looks like an aircrew but is a cluster of plane trees, a THICKET; 'to extract from' removes H.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail or bus pass you buy entitles you to travel, a permit to journey.

clue.text: Record King's time in power getting cut short

parts.note: regis is Latin for of the king, as in Rex and Regina

indicators.note: cutting a word short removes its final letter

parts.note: a term is a period in office

explanation.surface: A record of how a monarch's reign was ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the last letter of TERM to give TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A register is an official list or log, and as a verb or noun it means a record.

clue.text: Short of hope initially when cornered by dull fool

indicators.note: being cornered by something means being enclosed by it on both sides

parts.note: dead can mean dull or lifeless, as in a dead party
under means short of, as in under par

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of hope

explanation.surface: A hopeless fool trapped in a dreary corner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunderhead is a stupid person, a dimwit or idiot.

clue.text: English racecourse displacing first-rate course

indicators.note: displacing means the first-rate letters are pushed out of the racecourse name

parts.note: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National
A1 written AI means first-rate

explanation.surface: An English racecourse ousting a top-class track.
explanation.walkthrough: AINTREE is the English racecourse that hosts the Grand National; 'displacing' drops AI (A1, first-rate). 'course' is a dish, not a track.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a dish served at a meal, one course of the menu.

clue.text: Churchman mostly consuming core of sweet decoration Thanks Neil W. We're still here at the moment so thanks for the early comment!

indicators.note: consuming means the churchman word swallows the core letter
mostly means losing the last letter

parts.note: an Anglican is a member of the Church of England

indicators.note: the core of sweet is its central letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman eating the middle of a cake decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing thanks are blog text, not clue. ANGLICA ('mostly' drops N) takes in E, the core of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied green stems of this herb are used to decorate cakes and desserts.

clue.text: Information in computer language — here's list of items

indicators.note: the information word sits inside the language name

parts.note: Ada is a programming language named after Ada Lovelace
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Details on a programming language making up a list of items.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be discussed at a meeting.

clue.text: Horse, creature with siblings in rear group in Aintree

indicators.note: the quintuplet goes inside the closing letters of Aintree

parts.note: the rear group of letters in Aintree is its last pair
a quin is a quintuplet, born with four siblings

explanation.surface: A horse with stablemates running at the back at Aintree racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine means of the horse family, and used as a noun it names a horse.

clue.text: US State Department's closing message

parts.note: Tex. is an abbreviation for Texas
the closing letter of Department

explanation.surface: The US State Department's final communiqué.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State Department' reads as one name, but splits: TEX (Texas) + T, the end of 'Department'.
explanation.definitionFit: A text is a short message sent by phone.

clue.text: "Tell no-one castle and boat will carry computer stuff" — Duke

indicators.note: carrying means the castle-and-boat pair hold the other letters between them

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
the ark is Noah's boat
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A duke ordering secrecy over computer gear hidden in a castle and a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means keep something secret, not telling anybody.

clue.text: Host initially appeared in embrace of child and animal

indicators.note: being in the embrace of the child word means sitting inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of appeared

explanation.surface: A host appearing with a child and a pet in their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A male cat is a familiar household animal.

clue.text: Story fed to officer in charge that's not readily moved

indicators.note: being fed to a word means going inside it

parts.note: Capt is the abbreviation for captain
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: An unflappable officer being told a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Catalepsy is a trance with rigid limbs, so a person so afflicted stays fixed and cannot easily be stirred.

clue.text: Detective was wrong, becoming discouraged

parts.note: erred means made a mistake

explanation.surface: A detective's mistake leaves them disheartened.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: someone put off from acting has been dissuaded or discouraged.

clue.text: Full one tucking into 6? Not wholly

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside the shortened course word
not wholly means the last letter is missing

parts.note: 6 points to the answer at 6 down, a dish served at a meal
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone half-full, eating into the main course.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is 6-down; 'Not wholly' trims its last E, and I goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole or complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: One noticing daughter's abandoned coloured pen

indicators.note: abandoned means the daughter letter is left out

parts.note: a red marker is a coloured pen
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter leaving behind her coloured felt-tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who remarks observes or notices something, so one who notices fits.

clue.text: Most reliable placing confidence in English? On the contrary

indicators.note: placing with in seems to put confidence inside English
in marks the container relationship
on the contrary reverses which word goes inside which

parts.note: trust is confidence

explanation.surface: Whether the English are the most trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the instruction: E goes in TRUST, not TRUST in E.
explanation.definitionFit: True can mean loyal or dependable, so the superlative means most dependable.

clue.text: Regret and mastery mostly displayed in dry Western

indicators.note: displayed in means placed inside the dry word

parts.note: TT is teetotal, abstaining from drink
to rue is to regret

indicators.note: mostly means losing the last letter

parts.note: a grip on something is mastery of it

explanation.surface: Regret and skill on show in a dusty cowboy setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means teetotal here, TT, not arid; 'mostly' trims the last letter of the mastery word.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic John Wayne cowboy film, a Western.

clue.text: Time to forget about tail of extinct bird

indicators.note: about means around the tail letter

parts.note: to omit is to leave out or forget

indicators.note: the tail of extinct is its last letter

explanation.surface: Time to forget the tail of a bird that has died out.
explanation.walkthrough: OMIT goes around T, the tail of 'extinct'; 'extinct bird' is not a dodo.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird, a familiar name for the blue tit.

clue.text: Loose playing I encountered in second Italian tune

indicators.note: playing means the letters of loose are rearranged
encountered in means the I is met inside the second word

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A singer playing it loose in an Italian song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges the letters of 'Loose' into OSOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Neapolitan song, so an Italian melody.

clue.text: Head of school exhibits pledges

indicators.note: the head of school is its first letter

parts.note: wears means displays, as one exhibits clothes

explanation.surface: A headteacher putting school pledges on show.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to vow or promise solemnly.

clue.text: Silent about editor, one in TV, say

indicators.note: about means wrapped around the editor and one

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A quiet editor working in television.
explanation.definitionFit: Television is a communication channel, an example of a mass medium.

clue.text: Grass also observable in mirror?

indicators.note: reading the same in a mirror points to a word that is identical backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A grass that looks the same in a mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass that binds sand dunes.

clue.text: Reports air polluted? This may be needed

definitions.text: Reports air polluted? This may be needed

indicators.note: polluted means the letters of reports air are fouled into a new order

explanation.surface: News of dirty air means a breathing mask may be required.
explanation.definitionFit: A mask that filters dirty air, needed when the atmosphere is contaminated.

clue.text: One good between rugby posts, having senior ranking?

indicators.note: between means set inside the pair of posts

parts.note: rugby goalposts are shaped like the letter H, so two posts suggest two such letters
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A good kick between the posts earning a top rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby posts are H-shaped; I + G goes between two Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: High means elevated in rank or status, as in high office.

clue.text: Error in number provided by American

definitions.meaning: making a mess of something, a botch
Americans call the symbol for number the number sign, which Britons name after a chopped dish

explanation.surface: A mistake in a figure an American supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: A botched job is a mess, and the # sign stands for number in US usage.

clue.text: Queen leads me carrying fashionable garb for nobility

indicators.note: leads means the queen letters come first

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: carrying means the me word holds the fashionable word

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: The Queen leading me while carrying stylish robes for the peerage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ermine fur trims the robes of peers, a garment of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Chap's trickery's revolutionary, keeping number put out

indicators.note: keeping means holding the number letter inside
revolutionary means turned around, read backwards

parts.note: Tim's: Tim is a man's name, a chap
art means trickery or cunning

explanation.surface: A man's revolutionary cunning, keeping figures quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns TIMS + ART into TRASMIT; N goes in. 'Chap' stands for any man's name, here TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something out on air or a network is to broadcast or send it.
